source.section: PIT-ADJ instructions PDF page 7, line 25, Table 2 and Examples 1 and 2; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12; Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = private pension (person 0) 80,000.00 + taxable Social Security (85% of gross 60,000.00) 51,000.00 = 131,000.00. Federal taxable income = 131,000.00 - standard deduction 31,500.00 - 2 x 1,600.00 additional for age 65 or older = 96,300.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing jointly. Line 9 federal AGI 131,000.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 34,700.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 131,000.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 55,000.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15, PIT-ADJ: line 13 age 65 or older: Table 1 (married filing jointly) row for federal AGI 131,000.00 gives 0.00 x 2 qualifying = 0.00; line 25 Social Security: federal AGI 131,000.00 does not exceed the Table 2 maximum 150,000.00 (married filing jointly), so the 51,000.00 included in AGI is exempt = 51,000.00; PIT-ADJ line 28 total 51,000.00. Line 17 = 131,000.00 + 0.00 - 34,700.00 - 0.00 - 51,000.00 = 45,300.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 96,300.00 - 51,000.00 = 45,300.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 45,300.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 8,000.00 = 120 + 3.2% x 17,000.00 = 544 + 4.3% x 20,300.00 = 872.9; total 1,536.9, to the cent 1,536.90. The table row over 45,200 to 45,300 gives 1,535; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 1,536.90.
